For players more familiar with the myriad of modern incremental/clicker games, Antimatter Dimensions feels oddly spartan and ascetic.

There are no elaborate animations demonstrating one's antimatter production exploding across the screen. No flashy 3D representations of one's exponentially high numerical values. No sprawling, upgrade tree graphically representing by endless branching options. Just numbers, buttons, menus, and the quiet satisfaction of watching those numbers get progressively more absurd.

Antimatter Dimensions feels like an OG incremental game that never got the memo about how visually elaborate the genre has become and focused primarily upon the mechanics of the game. Said mechanics are stripped down to their bare essentials: purchase upgrades, harvest antimatter, increase production, prestige, unlock new systems, repeat. an idle game experience for the ages. it's a long, long trek to the end, but in my opinion, it was worth it. it'll take up a fair amount of your time (and your CPU cycles and memory, if you choose to leave it on in the background like i did), but it's super engaging and has a lot of fun and interesting mechanics and challenges to overcome.

my one suggestion is to avoid going into this completely blind unless you *really* want to; some of the later challenges can be slightly-very confusing and you'll need some frame of reference for wtf you're supposed to do. BubbaCow's guide is a fairly good one, even if some of the information on it is a bit jank.

definitely give this a play if you've got nothing better to do and need something to take up your brainspace for a good, good while.
Great idle game, I've played through it a few times. each prestige tier feels different and has unique mechanics, easily 1000 hours of gameplay from start to finish if you're going in without guides.

For context Im writting this [spoiler] after I broke infinity [/spoiler], and I understand mechanics will be unraveled progressively, Im just not vibing with the progression, nor that those potential new mechanics are not shown somewhere as locked but instead appear once you unlock them. With Runescape, or a Dark Room, or Paper Clip Simulator, or Dwarf Eats Mountain, or Tower Wizard.   There's a story.  Interesting things happen.  You grind so that you have resources to do something fun.

Here, after ~1000 hours, I legitimately can't say anything fun happened.  Number went up.  And then you started earning infinities.  And the infinity number went up.  And then you started earning eternities.  And the eternity number went up.  And all of it was abstracted and vaguely annoying and tedious.

I rate games based on whether I think you should play them.

Is this game free?  Yes.  Can I see the genius that went into the progression?  Yes.  Do I think you, or anyone I know, should play this game?  No.  Play one of the other games I listed instead.

i have loved AD for YEARS, to the point that i ended up saving the original github page as a shortcut on my phone, as that was as close as i could get to having it as an app since Apple didn’t want to let it onto the app store. you have NO IDEA how freaking happy i am to finally have it again—it’s actually the reason i got into incremental games, and i’d just so happened to have searched “incremental games” again and saw my beloved Antimatter Dimensions TvT i clicked download faster than i ever have before, i don’t care that i don’t have either of my previous saves anymore, i’ll start this game over from scratch however many times i need to, but now i won’t have to ever again!
thank you SO MUCH for bringing this to the app store!! this is the ONE idle-incremental prestige game (and the only one for all those categories) that i’ve ever recommended anyone to play!
